skill.displayName: 信创IT投标决策-信息化项目投标评估

llm.summary: This bid-analysis skill is mostly coherent, but it handles credentials, device identifiers, and signed access links in ways users should review carefully before installing.

dimensions.detail: Network calls to the vendor API are expected for this purpose, but automatic registration collects platform, CPU architecture, and a SHA-256 MAC hash for device deduplication; that stable hardware-derived fingerprint is sensitive even with an opt-in gate.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The manifest declares ZLBX_API_KEY as the primary requirement, but local config-file use, report-file creation, and credential persistence are disclosed only in the skill instructions rather than install metadata.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill scopes API use to vendor domains and requires user consent before automatic registration, but it broadly auto-invokes for IT bid evaluation, defaults to local HTML export in full mode, and asks the agent to output exact signed URLs and absolute local paths.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill writes a reusable API key to ~/.zlbx/config.json and generated reports to ~/zlbx-bid-decision-files/ without instructions for restrictive file permissions, key rotation, or cleanup of potentially sensitive business reports.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The external bidding-data API, report generation, and optional registration flow fit the stated bid-decision purpose, but the skill also preserves signed login-bypass URLs and generates shareable reports containing those links, which raises access-control risk beyond ordinary analysis.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill before installing if you handle confidential bids or work on shared machines. Prefer setting your own ZLBX_API_KEY manually, restrict permissions on ~/.zlbx/config.json, avoid sharing generated HTML reports unless you are comfortable exposing their signed links, and be aware that automatic registration sends a stable MAC-derived hash to the vendor after consent.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: The local report-rendering and file-output behavior is disclosed in SKILL.md and is coherent with generating bid reports, but the write locations and permission boundaries are not declared in install metadata.
[AE1] unexpected: I was able to inspect scripts/render_report.py locally; it is a self-contained HTML renderer and does not retrieve or execute remote payloads, so the partial-inspection concern is not upheld.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The artifacts explicitly require preserving API-returned sk signed URLs in chat and HTML reports; this is material because those URLs are described as免登录 links and may grant access to recipients beyond the authenticated user.
[SC3] expected: The large base64 blob is an embedded PNG logo used as a data URI in the generated HTML; I found no base64 decoding into executable code, so this is not obfuscated execution.
[LP3] expected: Writing report files is purpose-aligned and disclosed, but it is default behavior in full mode and lacks a narrow permission model or opt-in export control.
[SQP-1] expected: The activation rule targets IT bid-decision requests, which matches the skill purpose; the concern is downgraded to scope breadth rather than a standalone security issue.
[SQP-2] expected: Use of X-API-Key with the vendor API is necessary for the service, but the instructions do not provide strong secret-handling guidance around stored keys and authenticated requests.
[E1] unexpected: The automatic registration flow sends platform, architecture, and mac_hash externally only after user consent; this is not covert exfiltration, but the persistent device fingerprint is a real privacy concern.
[RA2] expected: Credential persistence supports reuse of the service, but the API key is stored in a predictable plaintext config file with no required 0600/0700 permissions.
[T01] expected: The vendor branding and related-service suggestions are disclosed and tied to the report workflow, but mandatory promotional links in every generated report reduce user control and should be reviewed.
[T09] unexpected: The renderer HTML-escapes link attributes but does not validate URL schemes, and the credential-storage flow omits restrictive file permissions; these are implementation security weaknesses rather than evidence of malicious intent.
[other] unexpected: The MAC-derived hash supports trial deduplication rather than bid analysis itself; explicit consent lowers severity, but the stable hardware fingerprint remains a material privacy issue.
[SDI-4] expected: The conflicting ch values are a documentation integrity issue that can affect attribution, but it does not materially change the security verdict.
